subtitle: When the Crown Fell, the Chariot Rolled On

panels.shot: low-angle, half-shadowed medium shot of Govinda Vidyadhara before the towering Jagannath temple at dusk
panels.action: Govinda Vidyadhara stands in the temple courtyard, one hand on his sword hilt and the other resting on the stone balustrade, as the spires of Jagannath rise behind him against a blood-red sky.

dialogue.text: In 1541, as the Suryavamsi crown fell in blood, a minister named Govinda Vidyadhara seized Orissa—yet the chariot of Jagannath rolled on without him.

i18n.hi: १५४१ में, जब रक्त में सूर्यवंशी ताज गिरा, गोविन्द विद्याधर नाम के मंत्री ने ओड़िशा छीन लिया — पर जगन्नाथ का रथ उसके बिना भी चलता रहा।

panels.shot: wide aerial view of Puri and Cuttack marked by distant silhouettes, with coastline and rivers glinting in the sun
panels.action: A sweeping vista shows the sacred town of Puri by the sea and the fortified city of Cuttack on the river, tiny amid forests and fields, under a hazy, humid sky.

dialogue.text: The mid-sixteenth century. Suryavamsi Orissa stretches from temple town to fort city, old power breathing unevenly through coastal plains, forests and river forts.

i18n.hi: सोलहवीं सदी का बीच। सूर्यवंशी ओड़िशा मन्दिर नगरों से क़िलों तक फैला, पुरानी सत्ता तट, जंगल और नदी-क़िलों में टुकड़ों में साँस ले रही है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the great Jagannath temple gopuram rising over crowded streets
panels.action: The towering spire of the Jagannath temple dominates the skyline of Puri, its stone dark with age, as pilgrims and servants move like ants in the streets below.

dialogue.text: At its heart stands Jagannath, Lord of the World. Around His temple, priests, cooks, carpenters, dancers and scribes live by the rhythm of daily ritual.

i18n.hi: बीचोंबीच जगन्नाथ खड़े हैं, जग के नाथ। उनके मन्दिर के चारों ओर पुजारी, रसोईये, बढ़ई, नर्तकी और लेखक रोज़ की सेवा की धुन पर जीते हैं।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Gajapati court in Cuttack, with throne slightly empty, courtiers in muted anxiety
panels.action: Inside the audience hall at Cuttack, a gilded throne stands under a canopy; nobles and officers cluster in uneasy groups, the air thick with whispers and uncertainty.

dialogue.text: Here the Gajapati once commanded armies and kings. But after Prataparudra withdraws from the world, the throne of Orissa no longer feels steady beneath its ornaments.

i18n.hi: यहीं कभी गजपति सेनाएँ और राजाओं को हुक्म देता था। पर प्रतापरुद्र के लोक से हटते ही, ओड़िशा का सिंहासन अपने गहनों के नीचे अस्थिर लगने लगा।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Govinda standing at the edge of the court, observing, half in shadow
panels.action: Govinda Vidyadhara, robed as a high minister, stands with folded hands near a court pillar, his sharp eyes watching the shifting faces of nobles and attendants.

dialogue.text: Among these men stands Govinda Vidyadhara, a powerful officer of the palace. The records name him minister, servant of the Gajapati, and soon, something more.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं लोगों के बीच खड़ा है गोविन्द विद्याधर, महल का ताक़तवर अफ़सर। लेखों में वह मंत्री है, गजपति का सेवक, और जल्द ही, कुछ और भी।

panels.shot: dim interior shot of a small shrine where a figure symbolizing Prataparudra sits or withdraws, distant from court
panels.action: In a secluded chamber lit by oil lamps, a royal figure sits before an image of Jagannath, head bowed, as attendants wait at a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Prataparudra Gajapati, last strong king of the Suryavamsis, withdraws from daily rule around 1540. Tradition says he turns more to pilgrimage and prayer than to council.

i18n.hi: प्रतापरुद्र गजपति, सूर्यवंश का आख़िरी मज़बूत राजा, लगभग १५४० में रोज़ के राजकाज से हट जाता है। परम्परा कहती है, वह सभा से ज़्यादा तीर्थ और जप की ओर मुड़ता है।

panels.shot: narrative montage shot: two brief ghost-like images of young kings on the throne, one after another, with a calendar in the background turning quickly
panels.action: A double image shows first one youthful king, then another, seated on the same throne as the pages of a painted calendar flip rapidly in the background.

dialogue.text: After him, the Madala Panji names Kalua Deva and Kakharua Deva. Two brief reigns, little power, their very details dim in the memory of chroniclers.

i18n.hi: उसके बाद मदला पंजी कळुआ देव और कखरुआ देव के नाम लिखती है। दो छोटे राज, कम ज़ोर, उनका ब्यौरा तक इतिहास की याद में धुँधला है।

panels.shot: close-up on Govinda’s face, lit by torchlight, expression set and unreadable
panels.action: Govinda Vidyadhara’s face fills the frame in flickering torchlight, jaw clenched, eyes hard, as the murmur of distant voices seems to press on him from the dark.

dialogue.text: Somewhere between these fragile kings and the restless nobility, the minister makes his choice. The chronicles do not record his words, only what he did.

i18n.hi: इन नाज़ुक राजाओं और बेचैन सरदारों के बीच कहीं मंत्री अपना फ़ैसला करता है। इतिहास में उसके बोल नहीं, सिर्फ़ उसका किया दर्ज है।

panels.shot: shadowy corridor wide shot, with Govinda advancing flanked by armed retainers, palace doors ahead
panels.action: In a dim palace corridor, Govinda strides forward with a small group of armed retainers, their footsteps frozen mid-stride as they move toward a guarded inner doorway.

dialogue.text: In 1541, Govinda Vidyadhara moves against his own lords. The Madala Panji is blunt—he has Kalua Deva and Kakharua Deva killed, and takes the crown.

i18n.hi: १५४१ में गोविन्द विद्याधर अपने ही स्वामियों पर चढ़ बैठता है। मदला पंजी सीधी बात कहती है — वह कळुआ देव और कखरुआ देव को मरवाता है, और ताज ले लेता है।

panels.shot: wide throne-room shot, Govinda seated on the Gajapati throne, nobles bowing, but some faces turned away
panels.action: Govinda now sits on the high throne beneath the royal canopy, a crown newly placed on his head, while some nobles bow and others glance at each other with guarded eyes.

dialogue.text: With that act, the Suryavamsi line ends not in peaceful ceremony, but in palace bloodshed. Govinda, once servant, now stands as founder of the Bhoi dynasty.

i18n.hi: इस वार से सूर्यवंशी वंश शान्त रस्म में नहीं, महल की खून-रेज़ी में खत्म होता है। गोविन्द, जो सेवक था, अब भोई वंश का संस्थापक बन खड़ा है।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind the throne, looking past Govinda toward the Jagannath temple banners visible through a window
panels.action: Seen from behind the throne, Govinda’s silhouette is framed against a distant view of Jagannath temple flags fluttering in the sea wind through an open window.

dialogue.text: Yet even as he claims the palace, the real centre lies a little distance away, where the banners of Jagannath fly over Puri, indifferent to court intrigue.

i18n.hi: पर जब वह महल हथियाता है, असली केन्द्र कुछ दूर है, जहाँ पुरी पर जगन्नाथ के ध्वज लहराते हैं, दरबारी साज़िशों से बेपरवाह।

panels.shot: busy temple courtyard wide shot, with sevayats preparing offerings and ordinary people moving purposefully
panels.action: In the courtyard of the Jagannath temple, sevayats grind spices, shape offerings and sweep the flagstones, as lines of pilgrims move past under the shade of stone colonnades.

dialogue.text: Here the temple society goes on. Cooks prepare the Mahaprasad, carpenters plan the next ratha, drummers and dancers drill their steps. The king may change; the seva does not pause.

i18n.hi: यहाँ मन्दिर की दुनिया चलती रहती है। रसोईये महाप्रसाद बनाते हैं, बढ़ई अगली रथ की योजना करते, ढोलिए और नर्तक कदम साधते हैं। राजा बदले, सेवा नहीं रुकती।

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes in a quiet chamber, writing on palm-leaf manuscripts by lamplight
panels.action: In a low-roofed room lined with palm leaves, two scribes sit cross-legged by oil lamps, pressing stylus-tips into fresh leaves, stacks of bound manuscripts beside them.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere in the land, Odia words continue their own kingdom. Sarala Das’s Mahabharata is copied, Odia Bhagabata recited, poets and pandits carrying stories beyond the walls of any court.

i18n.hi: धरती पर कहीं और, ओड़िया शब्द अपना अलग राज चलाते हैं। सरला दास की महाभारत नकल होती, ओड़िया भगवता गूँजती, कवि और पण्डित कथाएँ किसी भी दरबार से परे ले जाते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic street-level wide shot of the Ratha Yatra chariot rising above the crowd, ropes taut in many hands
panels.action: A towering wooden chariot, freshly painted, looms above a dense crowd as hundreds of hands grasp thick ropes, frozen in the moment before they heave together.

dialogue.text: Each year, the ratha of Jagannath is raised anew. Carpenters, painters, rope-makers and singers gather as one. Kings come and go, but the chariot still must move.

i18n.hi: हर वर्ष जगन्नाथ का रथ फिर से उठता है। बढ़ई, चित्रकार, रस्सी बनाने वाले, गायक सब जुटते हैं। राजा आएँ जाएँ, रथ तो चलना ही है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Paika soldiers drilling in a field, with small plots of land and huts visible nearby
panels.action: In an open field, Paika soldiers practice with spears and shields, their huts and small cultivated plots visible just beyond the training ground.

dialogue.text: The Paikas, village soldiers with service lands, still drill in the dust. Their grants bind them to temple and state alike, a web of duty that does not break overnight.

i18n.hi: पाइक, गाँवों के सेवा-जमींदार सिपाही, अभी भी धूल में दाव लगाते हैं। उनकी जागीर उन्हें मन्दिर और राज्य दोनों से बाँधती है, यह फ़र्ज़ रातों-रात नहीं टूटता।

panels.shot: medium shot of Govinda at a council table with maps, looking strained, candlelight casting long shadows
panels.action: Govinda leans over a low table strewn with maps and palm-leaf records, his brow furrowed, as councillors’ shadowed forms sit around him in the flicker of candlelight.

dialogue.text: Govinda must rule a kingdom already fraying. To the south, Vijayanagara watches; from the north and west, new Afghan and later Mughal powers advance. His usurpation brings a crown, not calm.

i18n.hi: गोविन्द को पहले से बिखरता राज सँभालना है। दक्षिण में विजयनगर नज़र रखे है; उत्तर-पश्चिम से नये अफ़गान, फिर मुग़ल बढ़ रहे हैं। उसकी गद्दी हथियाने से ताज मिला, चैन नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of Govinda in older age, looking out a window toward the sea, lines of care on his face
panels.action: An older Govinda stands by a high window, hands resting on the stone sill, gazing toward the faint glimmer of the distant sea, his face marked by fatigue and reflection.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_vidyadhara
dialogue.text: I took a throne, but what truly endures in this land?

i18n.hi: मैंने सिंहासन लिया, पर इस धरती में सच में टिकता क्या है?

panels.shot: montage wide shot: faint layered images of later turmoil—armies on the march, distant smoke over a temple city—set against Jagannath’s wheel symbol
panels.action: A faint montage shows distant armies marching and smoke rising over a city, all overlaid by a large, still image of Jagannath’s wheel symbol carved in stone.

dialogue.text: In decades after Govinda, harsher storms will come—Afghan generals, temple desecrations, new overlords. Yet records like Hermann Kulke’s show the Jagannath polity adapting, surviving beyond any one dynasty.

i18n.hi: गोविन्द के बाद के दशकों में और सख़्त तूफ़ान आयेंगे — अफ़गान सेनापति, मन्दिर तोड़ने वाले, नये स्वामी। पर हरमन कूल्के जैसे शोध बताते हैं कि जगन्नाथ का राज्य ढाँचा बदल कर भी, किसी एक वंश से आगे टिकता रहा।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Jagannath chariot rolling away into the horizon at sunset, silhouetted crowd behind it
panels.action: At sunset, Jagannath’s great chariot is seen from behind, slowly rolling down the avenue toward the horizon, a dark mass of devotees following in its shadow.

dialogue.text: Govinda Vidyadhara’s rise marks the twilight of Suryavamsi kings, but the land’s afterlife runs deeper—when crowns fall, it is the chariot, the song and the service that keep moving.

i18n.hi: गोविन्द विद्याधर का उभार सूर्यवंशी राजाओं की साँझ है, पर इस धरती का अगला जीवन और गहरा है — ताज गिरते हैं, रथ, गीत और सेवा ही चलते रहते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Crown Fell, the Chariot Rolled On
